title: Extension by zero preserves products and derived limits
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$
be a quasi-compact open immersion with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$
and $B$ a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then:

1. for every $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},j^*B)$ there is a distinguished
triangle, functorial in $K$,
$$
j_!K\longrightarrow Rj_*K\longrightarrow i_*i^*Rj_*K\longrightarrow j_!K[1];
$$
2. $j_!:D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},j^*B)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$ preserves
products and derived inverse limits $R\varprojlim$ of sequences;
3. on module sheaves, $j_!$ preserves products.

The coefficients on $U$ and $Z$ are the inverse images $j^*B$ and $i^*B$. The exact sheaf functors $j_!,i^*,i_*$ also denote their termwise induced functors on unbounded derived categories [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; $Rj_*$ is total right derived direct image [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Products are small products [def-weil-category-product], and a sequential derived limit means an object with a distinguished Roos triangle as in [def-weil-derived-limit].

external.place: *(2) Products and derived limits.* The pro-étale topos is replete, so products of sheaves are exact (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 3.1.10); hence the product in $D(-_{\mathrm{proét}})$ of a family of complexes is represented by the termwise product.

*(2) Products and derived limits.* The pro-étale topos is replete, so products of sheaves are exact (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 3.1.10); hence the product in $D(-_{\mathrm{proét}})$ of a family of complexes is represented by the termwise product.

proof.text: For the natural triangle, apply lem-sf-exact-localization-derived-triangle to F=j_!, S=j^*, G=j_* and H=i_*i^*. The open-closed sequence supplies exactness, both arrows, their zero composite, and short exactness. The open direct-image counit is invertible: open restriction is fully faithful, and the module counit reflects its abelian carrier. Grothendieck module categories supply functorial K-injective replacements. Exact-functor descent and the chosen total derived functor have precisely the definitions in the target.

Prove that a functor which is naturally the kernel of a map between product-preserving functors preserves products, by constructing the unique lift with the two product universal properties and the kernel universal property. Apply this to j_!j^*, id and i_*i^*: the sheaf sequence identifies the first with the kernel, and closed inverse image preserves products. Since j^* is product preserving and essentially surjective (the open-extension unit is invertible), transport product preservation from j^* composed with j_! to j_!. This includes empty products.

Use lem-sf-proetale-module-object-products-exact on U and X. The existing DerivedCategory.Q preservation instance from WeilConjectures.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TowerLimit makes localization preserve products for these categories. Termwise j_! preserves products by the preceding step; mapDerivedCategoryFactors identifies localization followed by derived j_! with termwise j_! followed by localization. Essential surjectivity of Q transports product preservation to derived j_!.

For a sequence K and transitions t, construct the image product using preservation, and write e for the canonical comparison. Composing with each projection proves F.map(towerProductShift t) composed with e equals e composed with the image shift. Additivity gives the same identity for 1-shift. Map the supplied distinguished Roos triangle through the triangulated derived functor and transport its two product terms through e, checking all three triangle squares. This is the required image derived limit. Use the equivalence between Discrete(ULift N) and Discrete N to specialize the universe-sized product preservation.

split_report.summary: Rebuilt the earlier attempt after checking all cited statements. Expanded the original referenced setting to state X qcqs explicitly; retained arbitrary, possibly noncommutative ring-sheaf coefficients. Added existing general Grothendieck/K-injective, natural complex-SES triangle and exact-derived-functor tools. Proved sheaf products by a kernel calculation, derived products termwise, and derived-limit preservation by an explicit projection calculation on the Roos triangle. Removed the inapplicable adic-coefficient exact-functor/Rlim citation and placeholder quotes. No new nodes. Second reader: cited the existing universe convention explicitly and independently repeated semantic, type-pattern and source searches; retained all five mathematical steps.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 supplies the foundations used in proof (1); Step 2 realizes its triangle and naturality. Step 3 proves proof (3) directly using the exact sheaf sequence, Step 4 realizes the product part of (2), and Step 5 realizes the Roos-fibre part of (2). The unit and chapter route are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Generic Grothendieck property for modules over arbitrary ring sheaves; the closed-unit unit supplies no such foundation.
Generic K-injective existence needed to compute unbounded Rj_*; not an alternative to any closed-unit argument.
Generic full faithfulness of K-injective representatives, needed for derived naturality.
The blueprint explicitly requires product preservation of closed inverse image for arbitrary ring-sheaf coefficients.
Generic termwise representation of derived products over an arbitrary pro-etale ring sheaf; this is the exact product input in the blueprint.
Generic existence and uniqueness up to isomorphism of a Roos limit once the product exists; no adic hypotheses or tower-category coefficient identification.

lean.statement: theorem proEtale_openExtension_products_derivedLimits {X Z U : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] (hU : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ) (B : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj B] : (∃ (a : ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B ⟶ ringSheafDerivedDirectImage j B) (b : ringSheafDerivedDirectImage j B ⟶ ringSheafDerivedDirectImage j B ⋙ ringSheafDerivedClosedLocalization i j hU B) (c : ringSheafDerivedDirectImage j B ⋙ ringSheafDerivedClosedLocalization i j hU B ⟶ ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B ⋙ shiftFunctor (ringSheafDerivedCategory X B) (1 : ℤ)), ∀ K, Triangle.mk (a.app K) (b.app K) (c.app K) ∈ distTriang (ringSheafDerivedCategory X B)) ∧ (∀ I : Type (u + 1), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B)) ∧ (∀ (K : ℕ → ringSheafDerivedCategory U ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} j).obj B)) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, K (n + 1) ⟶ K n) [HasProduct K] (L : ringSheafDerivedCategory U ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} j).obj B)), IsDerivedLimit t L → Exists fun [hP : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ (ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B).obj (K n))] ↦ IsDerivedLimit (K := fun n : ℕ ↦ (ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B).obj (K n)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B).map (t n)) ((ringSheafDerivedOpenExtension j B).obj L)) ∧ (∀ I : Type (u + 1), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (ringSheafOpenExtension j B))
lean.note: The recorded canonical arbitrary-ring module-object functors are used. Derived categories use HasDerivedCategory.standard. The closed term is termwise descent of the exact composite i_* i^*, avoiding an independent closed-stratum localization choice. All helper definitions have real data from the recorded exactness theorem, the Grothendieck K-injective construction and the recorded total right derived universal pair. Natural transformations express functoriality of the triangle; small products have index universe u+1.
